I hope that it's ok to ask this here. I see no subverse for Skyrim specific modding and the Skyrim subverse is pretty much dead.

Seeing as the average mod author on the Nexus seems to be a complete fucking crybaby and the comments are locked on the Tes5edit page for that very reason, I hope that someone here can answer a question or two about it. If all else fails I'll dig through the documentation although that's a last resort because I honestly don't want to waste my time reading about all the things I already know just to find the one thing that I don't know.

Lately my mission has been to manually merge smaller mods into my own large mod. At first I was using the buggy and frustrating Creation Kit entirely for this. Then I realised that I can quite easily copy content over in Tes5edit. The two main options I've been using are 'copy' and 'override'. However, seemingly randomly, it sometimes wants to make the mod I am trying to eliminate a master of the mod I'm trying to copy the content into. In this case I go back to using the Creation Kit and copy the data exactly as it is, no mess, no masters, no fuss.

What I want to know is, is there a way to copy this data with Tes5edit without it worrying about masters? I just want it to copy across the forms exactly as is, even if I have to perform a few manual edits afterwards. Could I achieve this perhaps with the 'deep copy' option? Is there another tool that would be better for this job?

On a side note, I was starting to think that Tes5edit is the best possible modding tool for Skyrim. How disappointed I was to go to it's page on Nexus only to see the author complaining and complaining and complaining, mentioning how they never play Skyrim and they can't handle all the people who do. In that case I feel like they can just stick their Tes5edit far up their asses.

Sometimes I honestly wish that Bethesda didn't support modding and that it was a smaller community with less whine bags. I just think of the modding tools for actual complete and non-buggy games like Fable TLC or Pokémon third gen. The tools available for those games are streamlined and fixed up to the nth degree. And that is because they are created and maintained by the community. But in Skyrim we have the Creation Kit. And like anything Bethesda does it's buggy as hell and we can only dream about it getting fixed or maintained by those clowns. And thanks to it's existence there will never be a community made tool to rival it.

I love Skyrim but I hate the bugs and I hate the fact that Bethesda just expects their customers to fix all of their fuck ups. Imagine that Nike released a new pair of shoes that people in their multitudes buy. But after two weeks the soles are starting to come loose on those pairs of shoes. But instead of Nike refunding those customers or replacing that product, they send a repair kit with a hammer, some nails and a bottle of glue and say "fix it yourselves". Then you try to fix it yourself only to discover that the hammer head keeps falling off it's handle, the nails are all bent and the glue is dried up. That is the situation with Bethesda, Skyrim and the Creation Kit. And I wonder how they get away with it. Minus the bugs it really is an incredible game but it still surprises me that people seem to worship them so much and exempt them from any discussions about bad software companies.
